It enables durable, high-rate sodium-ion batteries, offering a pathway to sustainable energy storage through mechanically robust, dynamically volume-adjusting cathode materials.

ACS Nano | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using a machine-learning-powered soft-templating protocol to generate disordered carbon models with controlled pore sizes, isolating confinement effects from disorder. Significance: constant-potential simulations show capacitance rises as pores shrink below 1 nm at fixed disorder, reconciling confinement- and disorder-based views and offering unified design principles for supercapacitors.

💡 This work is novel in using tris(4-fluorophenyl)phosphine (TFPP) with a tailored formation protocol to control residual monomer degradation in in-situ gel polymer electrolytes. item.title: Escaping the Polymerization-Kinetics Trap in Ether Electrolytes for Durable Silicon Interphases
item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in identifying a polymerization-kinetics trap: stronger polymerization in trioxane electrolytes worsens silicon interphase durability by depleting species prematurely. Adding LiNO3 suppresses early trioxane activation while enabling nitrate-derived passivation, yielding a thinner, coherent interphase. This kinetic regulation significantly improves cycling stability, offering a new design principle for durable silicon anodes.
